drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What is the main problem: low mood, anxiety, panic, trouble sleeping, hearing or seeing things, racing thoughts, or something else?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the main mental health complaint guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: When did this start, and has it been getting better, worse, or staying the same?
questions.rationale: Onset and course distinguish acute crisis from a longer episode.

questions.text: Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, hopeless, or much less interested in things you usually enjoy?
questions.rationale: Core mood and anhedonia questions screen for a depressive episode.

questions.text: Do you feel anxious, on edge, or unable to stop worrying most days?
questions.rationale: Generalized anxiety is a common primary complaint and co-occurs with depression.

questions.text: Do you get sudden episodes of pounding heart, shortness of breath, or a sense you might die or lose control?
questions.rationale: Panic attacks can mimic cardiac or respiratory emergencies.

questions.text: How is your sleep: trouble falling asleep, waking too early, sleeping too much, or nightmares?
questions.rationale: Sleep change is a core feature of mood, anxiety, and trauma-related illness.

questions.text: Has your appetite or weight changed without you trying?
questions.rationale: Appetite and weight shifts support a mood or medical contributor.

questions.text: Have you had low energy, trouble concentrating, or felt slowed down or restless?
questions.rationale: Energy and concentration affect safety, work, and treatment planning.

questions.text: Have you been more irritable, angry, or snapping at people than usual?
questions.rationale: Irritability can be the main face of depression, mania, or trauma.

questions.text: Have you had thoughts of wanting to die, or of harming yourself? If so, do you have a plan or intent?
questions.rationale: Active suicidal thoughts with plan or intent need urgent attention.

questions.text: Have you hurt yourself on purpose, such as cutting or burning, even if you did not want to die?
questions.rationale: Nonsuicidal self-injury raises risk and needs a safety plan.

questions.text: Have you had thoughts of harming someone else, or do you feel you might lose control and hurt someone?
questions.rationale: Homicidal ideation or loss of control is a safety emergency.

questions.text: Have you heard voices, seen things others do not, or felt that people are watching or controlling you?
questions.rationale: Hallucinations or paranoia may indicate psychosis and need prompt assessment.

questions.text: Have you had stretches of needing much less sleep, talking fast, spending a lot, or feeling unusually powerful?
questions.rationale: Manic features change diagnosis and med safety.

questions.text: Have you been through something frightening or violent, and do memories, nightmares, or jumpiness still bother you?
questions.rationale: Trauma history points toward PTSD and informs a safer interview.

questions.text: How much alcohol, cannabis, or other drugs have you been using, and has that changed recently?
questions.rationale: Substances commonly cause or worsen mood, anxiety, and psychosis.

questions.text: Are you shaking, sweating, seizing, or feeling very sick after cutting back on alcohol or drugs?
questions.rationale: Alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal can be medically dangerous.

questions.text: Are you able to eat, drink, take medicines, and keep yourself safe at home right now?
questions.rationale: Inability to care for basic needs is a psychiatric emergency.

questions.text: Is there anyone at home who can stay with you, or are you isolated right now?
questions.rationale: Social support changes disposition and safety planning.

questions.text: Have you had depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or a psychiatric hospitalization before?
questions.rationale: Prior illness and hospitalizations raise relapse and risk.

questions.text: Does anyone in your family have depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or has anyone died by suicide?
questions.rationale: Family history informs risk and diagnosis.

questions.text: Are you taking any psychiatric medicines, and have you started, stopped, or missed doses recently?
questions.rationale: Missed doses, new meds, and withdrawal from psychotropics often explain new symptoms.

questions.text: Have you had a recent illness, thyroid problem, head injury, or new medical diagnosis?
questions.rationale: Medical causes can present as mood, anxiety, or psychosis.

questions.text: How is this affecting your work, school, relationships, or daily activities?
questions.rationale: Functional impact guides urgency and treatment intensity.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Suicidal thoughts with plan or intent
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe wanting to die, a suicide plan, or intent to harm themselves?

red_flags.label: Active self-harm
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report currently hurting themselves on purpose or feeling unable to stop?

red_flags.label: Thoughts of harming others
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report thoughts of harming someone else or fear of losing control and hurting someone?

red_flags.label: Possible psychosis
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe hearing voices, seeing things others do not, or feeling watched or controlled?

red_flags.label: Possible alcohol or drug withdrawal
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report shaking, sweating, seizures, or severe sickness after cutting back on alcohol or drugs?

red_flags.label: Unable to meet basic needs
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient say they cannot eat, drink, take medicines, or keep themselves safe at home?

red_flags.label: Possible mania
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe little need for sleep with racing thoughts, risky spending, or feeling unusually powerful?
